title: Hadfield Casino
summary: Written entirely in Python with no additional assets. Complete with progression system, unlocks, themes, and detailed statistics. Want to learn how to count cards? I've got you covered.
body:
## Requirements
Will run on literally anything that supports python. Even got it running on XP without much trouble. No pre-requisites! 

## Background
When most people turn 18 they're typically excited about finally being able to (legally) go to the pub. For me, it was being able to set foot in card rooms and casinos. 

I've been an avid poker player since I was 16, it's a beautiful game - the perfect mix of strategy and psychology. A byproduct of this hobby means spending a lot of time in casinos, and being tempted by the table games, where the house always wins. 

## Goals

While the house always wins, how much they win depends on how well you play. If you play blackjack perfectly the house edge is only 0.5%, playing poorly? 5%. Hitting on 17 against a dealer 2? All of the percents. 

What I wanted, was a place to learn the games and practice them. I had some requirements:
- Common UK side bets
- Accurate UK paytables
- Configurable blackjack shoe size
- Progressive jackpots

I couldn't find anything on the internet that even got close (everything is American) so I built my own.

::figure[screenshot-20260927-130129]

## Feature creep
What started off as a handful of casino games I could practice, ballooned into a fully fledged single player game, with features such as: 
- Multiple users on the same install
- Detailed player statistics
- Achievements and unlocks (new games, themes, overlays, card styles)
- A full progression system (optional)
- Strategy overlays
- Blackjack card counting
- Linked progressive jackpots
- 8 games, with additional table variations

## How it works

Most of the core logic is reusable across games, like the hand evaluation function. Even in non-poker games, often a lot of the side bets are evaluated using standard poker hand rankings. Blackjack's 21+3 sidebet is the same evaluation as a three card poker hand.


```python
def evaluate_three_card_hand(cards) -> HandEval:
    if len(cards) != 3:
        raise ValueError("Three card poker hands must contain exactly 3 cards.")

    values = sorted((c.value for c in cards), reverse=True)
    is_flush = len({c.suit for c in cards}) == 1
    is_straight, straight_high = _check_straight(values)
    counts = Counter(values)
    count_sizes = sorted(counts.values(), reverse=True)

    if is_straight and is_flush:
        assert straight_high is not None  # _check_straight always pairs True with a value
        return (STRAIGHT_FLUSH, HAND_NAMES[STRAIGHT_FLUSH], (straight_high,))
    if count_sizes[0] == 3:
        return (THREE_OF_A_KIND, HAND_NAMES[THREE_OF_A_KIND], (values[0],))
    if is_straight:
        assert straight_high is not None  # _check_straight always pairs True with a value
        return (STRAIGHT, HAND_NAMES[STRAIGHT], (straight_high,))
    if is_flush:
        return (FLUSH, HAND_NAMES[FLUSH], tuple(values))
    if count_sizes[0] == 2:
        pair_value = next(v for v, c in counts.items() if c == 2)
        kicker = next(v for v, c in counts.items() if c == 1)
        return (PAIR, HAND_NAMES[PAIR], (pair_value, kicker))
    return (HIGH_CARD, HAND_NAMES[HIGH_CARD], tuple(values))
```
## Statistics and achievements
Each hand played is tracked and evaluated along with cumulative house edge statistics. You can see how many hands you played correctly, how many you got wrong, and what your overall winrate is. 
::figure[screenshot-20260927-133656]

## Sample Gameplay - Three Card Poker

The first game I made, very simple (optimal strategy is to play Q-6-4 or better, and fold everything else). The Prime sidebet pays out if all player cards are the same colour. There are instances where you would fold a hand that wins this bet, so I made an animation to place these cards under the bet as would typically be done in a casino.

::figure[screencast-20260927-131758]
